A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TSPulse research work, with 37 pages including Appendices A.1–A.14. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–37 are unchanged; the differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original TSPulse experiments on anomaly detection, classification, imputation and retrieval, together with ablations, embedding sensitivity analyses and runtime measurements in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TSPulse experimental results in Sections 4–5 and the appendices. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain identical architecture and procedures, including dual-space reconstruction, dual embeddings, TSLens, hybrid masking and multi-head triangulation. No method component, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: The Monash/LibCity pre-training data and evaluation coverage are unchanged: TSB-AD anomaly detection, 29 UEA classification datasets, six LTSF imputation datasets, and synthetic/UCR-based retrieval scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Table 3 and the corresponding result tables. For example, both retain MOMENT, VQShape and UniTS in classification, and MOMENT and Chronos in retrieval.

E3.justification: The pre-training configurations, data splits, hyperparameter selection, masking regimes, model variants, retrieval augmentations and evaluation metrics remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices A.6–A.13.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, imputation masking analyses, retrieval augmentation tests and embedding sensitivity experiments, including Table 1 and Figures 9–14. No analytical question or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Run and seed information, statistical estimation procedures and uncertainty reporting are unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 7 retains TSPulse zero-shot/fine-tuned VUS-PR scores of 0.48/0.52 for univariate and 0.36/0.39 for multivariate anomaly detection.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, reconstruction losses, FFT formulation and anomaly-scoring equation remain identical in Section 2 and Appendices A.2, A.7 and A.8. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The scientific contribution and performance claims in the abstract, introduction and conclusion are unchanged. The revised release statement concerns resource access rather than a new scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of dual-space learning, embedding robustness and experimental performance are unchanged. Appendix A.14 retains the same limitations and future directions, including forecasting, few-shot classification and incremental learning.

D1.justification: v1's abstract promises that models and source code will be open-sourced soon. v2 reports their release under the Apache License and adds a Hugging Face access hyperlink. Implementation details are unchanged, and Appendix A.1 still describes reviewer ZIP access and a future public release.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in the introduction and Appendix A.3 are identical. The added resource hyperlink introduces no related work or revised novelty claim.

P1.justification: Only the abstract's final release sentence is rewritten, alongside the updated arXiv version/date stamp. Terminology, section organization and the remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and their placement are unchanged. Pages 2–37 render identically, while page 1 retains its layout around the edited sentence and version stamp.

improvement.justification: The new access link and Apache License statement modestly improve resource discoverability and reproducibility guidance over v1's release promise. Scientific content is unchanged. The benefit is limited by Appendix A.1's inconsistent future-release wording, and the PDFs alone do not establish whether the linked materials are complete or usable.
